title: Distinguish additive noise from a variational bottleneck

blocks.text: Additive noise perturbs a representation; a variational bottleneck also pays KL toward a prior. The task is: Implement additive or variational Gaussian bottleneck sampling with caller-supplied standard-normal noise. Without logvar return h+sigma*noise and zero KL; with logvar treat h as mu and return reparameterized z plus mean per-example KL to N(0,I). Evaluation returns the mean in either mode; noise and input shapes match.

The inputs are `h`, `noise`, `sigma`, `logvar`, `training`. Keep their roles separate while you trace the solution. The animation follows the supplied implementation, so every highlighted operation connects to code you can inspect.
